hint.label: Celts vs Britons
hint.text: The Celts were many different peoples spread all across Western and Central Europe at the time. The people living in modern-day England and Wales were more specifically known as Britons, but even they were split across lots of tribes!

atoms.b: The ((++people animals)) in Britain were called Celts or Britons. They were not one single group, but lived in many different tribes.
The Britons lived in villages with small houses made from materials like ((++wood would)), clay and thatch.
Another common type of settlement was called a hillfort. These were built on ((++high low)) ground to defend against attack.

feedback.finish: Unlike in the larger Roman cities, the Britons did not make buildings with stone.

feedback.correct: The Britons used rivers to get drinking water and to bathe, so it was important to be close to one.
A wooden wall was built around the settlement. Tribes would also dig ditches into the sides of the hill to make it more defensible.

atoms.hint: The chief would always have the largest home in a settlement.

feedback.correct: The chief’s house would often serve as a place for the community to gather.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The only large structures the Britons had were circles made out of massive, standing stones. The most famous example is Stonehenge, but historians still don’t know exactly what it was used for. Most likely, it was a place for religious rituals and feasts.

Stonehenge was built over a long period of time, long before the Romans came to Britain. The first stones were placed in around 2600 BC, but it wasn’t completed for another 1,000 years. Many of the stones were brought across from Wales and, even more amazingly, the central Altar Stone comes all the way from northern Scotland!

atoms.a: What was Stonehenge probably used for?
When did the Britons start building Stonehenge?
Where did the central Altar Stone come from?

feedback.finish: While we don’t know for sure what the stone circles were used for, the fact that stones were brought from so far away tells us that they were very important and that the people were very organised!
